working_title: Balance the Picnic Raft! | Otter Rhyme for Kids
visual_system: cinematic 3D-cartoon-inspired riverside tableaux with explicit start/action/end keyframes
interaction_style: repeatable balance chorus plus two gentle point-to-the-centre prompts
creative_intent: A warm, buoyant preschool rhyme in which one clearly staged action at a time teaches left, right, centre and balance through safe teamwork.

motion_language.easing: ease-out for entrances, ease-in-out for repositioning, slight 8 percent overshoot only on light props
motion_language.transition_family: hard cut on action with two motivated ripple match-cuts
motion_language.hierarchy: one hero action, one supporting reaction, low-contrast river ambience
motion_language.restraint: no whole-frame-only motion, no constant character bobbing, no flashing, no pose dissolves

music.arc: curious invitation, cautious imbalance, bright discovery, careful teamwork, confident chorus, gentle suspense, flowing relief, patient landing, full picnic chorus and six-second resolve

composition.focal_rule: one primary face or physical balance action near a thirds power point
composition.layers: background river ambience 0.2x, midground raft and friends 0.6x, foreground hero prop/action 1.0x
composition.camera_rule: one slow push, pan or follow per shot; never stack push, pan and rotation

quality_requirements: Each of the nine scenes has reviewed start, action and end visual states sampled from the encoded master.
Ollie, Willa, Fern, clothing, raft, basket, jug, blanket and river geography retain identity.
The raft remains double-tied for all dockside loading, boarding and unloading actions.
All three loads crowd left before the jug moves right; the raft visibly returns level before boarding.
Fern remains fully inside during the mild mid-river tilt and returns to centre before paddling.
The picnic appears only after unloading; the full musical payoff occurs only in scene 9.
Narration is one consistent Ana voice, no faster than 125 weighted WPM, with at least 0.6 seconds between phrases.
Audio passes -65 dB opening high-frequency hiss ceiling, -14 to -18 LUFS integrated loudness and true peak no higher than -1 dBTP.
Timeline is continuous, end card is final-only, full FFmpeg decode passes and all four contact-sheet families are manually reviewed.
